bear_case: Warsh's confirmation that the July 28 FOMC is a live rate-hike meeting — 'inflation too high,' 'prices too high,' rate decision 'in four weeks,' no forward guidance — represents the structural risk the July 1 dual gate clearance missed pricing. Rate futures at ~33% July hike probability imply the market has partially repriced, but a hot NFP today would sharply accelerate that move. The 10Y yield is testing 4.47–4.50% this morning — the ceiling prior briefings flagged explicitly as dangerous for Nasdaq multiples at P/E ~28x — and a two-standard-deviation NFP print above 150K could push yield firmly above 4.50%, bring July hike probability above 50%, and render July 1's dual gate clearance a false breakout before the 3-day holiday gap provides any ability to respond. The Nikkei's −2.47% decline on Asia semiconductor selloff is the clearest current signal that profit-taking in the AI/semis complex is not finished; H1's 80%+ semiconductor gains leave a large distributable float. NVDA at $197.18 — below the $200 gate despite yesterday's three-criteria clearance — is the tape confirming the semis-led rally has not yet established a durable floor. Invalidation: NFP prints 80–120K (Goldilocks), wages +0.2–0.3%, unemployment ≤4.3% — July hike probability falls toward 15%, 10Y retreats below 4.35%, NVDA reclaims $200, and the July 7 open with SPCX Nasdaq-100 forced buying ($7.3B combined with Russell) becomes the highest-conviction long entry of Q3. If SPX holds >7,460 AND VIX stays <17 through July 7, the dual gate clearance is confirmed as a sustained breakout and the bear case formally closes.
